Article Title: ‘Thank you for free publicity’: Dipke on cockroach effigy being burnt alongside Ravan on Dussehra
Article Text:
Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee is set to burn the cockroach effigy alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad at its grounds in Pitampura.

What has the committee said?

How did ‘cockroach’ become a political name?

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder, Abhijeet Dipke, on Monday took a sarcastic dig at the planned burning of a 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy alongside Ravan during Dussehra celebrations on October 20 in Delhi, saying, “Thank you for the free publicity. ”The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee is set to burn the cockroach effigy alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad at its grounds in Pitampura. The preparation for the event is underway, with the committee saying the initiative is intended to spread awareness about cleanliness and unhygienic conditions.Ashok Goel Devaraha, president of the Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee and BJP MLA from Model Town, said the cockroach effigy was meant to symbolise filth and reinforce the message of the triumph of good over evil.Devaraha told ANI that the committee had previously burnt effigies representing issues such as Naxalism and terrorism. This year, it chose a cockroach to highlight the need to eliminate dirt and unhygienic conditions from homes, neighbourhoods and society.He also denied that the decision was politically motivated, saying the initiative aligned with the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns.The planned effigy comes amid the rise of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a movement that emerged following remarks by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant during a Supreme Court hearing on May 15.The CJI had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees who become social media or RTI activists to “cockroaches” attacking the system.The remarks triggered a backlash among young people and inspired the CJP movement. The CJI later said his oral remarks had been “misquoted” and used with “malicious intent”.The CJP has since staged protests against former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and is now demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee is set to burn the cockroach effigy alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad. The preparation for the event is underway, with the committee saying the initiative is intended to spread awareness about cleanliness and unhygienic conditions.

Article Title: 'Highly inspiring': PM Modi hails Mohan Bhagwat's speech on RSS Sthapana Divas
Article Text:
During the RSS centenary celebrations in Nagpur, Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Mohan Bhagwat's impactful speech.

Bhagwat highlights RSS’s century-long journey

RSS chief speaks on Panch Parivartan and Swadeshi

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday praised Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat ’s speech at the organisation’s centenary Vijayadashami celebrations in Nagpur, noting his focus on national development, social harmony, self-reliance and nation-building.Describing the address as “very motivating”, PM Modi said Bhagwat had covered several important subjects, including the need to strengthen society and promote self-reliance.In a post on X, the prime minister also highlighted Bhagwat’s remarks on the spirit of service and nation-building among RSS volunteers, along with the organisation’s initiative known as panch parivartan.“Particularly noteworthy was his emphasis on the commitment to Seva and nation building that is integral to every RSS Swayamsevak. He also spoke about the panch parivartan and how these can contribute meaningfully to positive social change,” PM Modi wrote.The RSS marked its centenary Vijayadashami celebrations at Reshimbagh Ground in Nagpur, bringing its year-long commemorative programme towards its conclusion.Addressing the gathering, Bhagwat remembered Sant Ravidas, Swami Shraddhanand and Swami Lakshmanananda Saraswati, highlighting their contributions to spiritual devotion, social harmony and the preservation of religious values.He said the organisation had spent the past century seeking to awaken self-awareness and strengthen India’s unity and identity.“Remembering them is also appropriate because the work that the Sangh has been carrying out for the past 100 years is precisely aimed at awakening this self-awareness. On the foundation of that self-awareness, identity, and ethos, it strives to make India united and strong,” Bhagwat said.Bhagwat also discussed Panch Parivartan, highlighting self-awareness and the adoption of Swadeshi as key elements of the initiative.Referring to the concept, he said self-awareness was reflected in the Preamble to the Indian Constitution, particularly its opening words, “We, the people of India”.“As our Prant Sanghchalak ji mentioned in his introductory remarks regarding panch parivartan, one of its key aspects is practising self-awareness and adoption of Swadeshi. This self-awareness is reflected in the preamble of our Constitution, where we refer to ourselves as 'We, the people of India',” he said.The RSS was founded in Nagpur by Keshav Hedgewar, its first Sarsanghchalak, on Vijayadashami in 1925. The organisation has observed the festival annually since its establishment.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat’s speech at the organisation's centenary Vijayadashami celebrations in Nagpur. Describing the address as ‘very motivating’, PM Modi said Bhag Wat had covered several important subjects, including the need to strengthen society.

Article Title: ‘Rural safety net under attack’: Jairam Ramesh calls MGNREGA replacement a ‘surgical strike’
Article Text:
Ramesh referred to drought conditions in Beed and other districts of Maharashtra

Jairam ramesh alleges wage theft, fake attendance

MGNREGA replaced by vb-g ram g act

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday called the replacement of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with the VB-G RAM G Act a “surgical strike” on the social safety net protecting rural India, alleging that the move had weakened support for workers facing distress.In a post on X, Ramesh referred to drought conditions in Beed and other districts of Maharashtra, which he said were facing their worst drought in a decade. He said MGNREGA had provided a guarantee of support to rural workers during such crises, but alleged that its replacement had undermined that protection.“Beed and other districts in Maharashtra are facing the worst drought in a decade. MGNREGA was the guarantee of support in such times of extreme distress. But its replacement with VB-G RAM G is nothing less than a surgical strike on the social safety net that protected rural India,” he wrote.Ramesh also cited a field-level investigation published by a media outlet, alleging that villagers had not received work for months despite official records showing them as employed.He claimed that local politicians were pocketing workers’ wages and alleged that similar cases involving fake attendance and clone application scams had been reported in Uttar Pradesh and other BJP-ruled states.“This is not just corruption, but systemic theft of workers’ wages,” Ramesh said, accusing the government of presiding over what he called the theft of rural wages.The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, or VB-G RAM G Act, came into effect on July 1 after being passed during Parliament’s Winter Session in 2025.The legislation replaced MGNREGA’s 100-day employment guarantee with a 125-day guarantee. However, the Opposition has criticised the new law over the removal of Mahatma Gandhi’s name from the scheme and the introduction of a 60:40 Centre-State funding arrangement.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh called the replacement of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with the VB-G RAM G Act a ‘surgical strike’ on the social safety net protecting rural India. He said the move had weakened support for workers facing distress. He claimed that local politicians were pocketing workers’ wages.

Article Title: 'No double standards on terrorism': Rajnath Singh's stern warning at SCO meet with Pakistan at the table
Article Text:
‘Entire terror ecosystem must be dismantled’: Rajnath Singh at SCO meet with Ishaq Dar present

Rajnath meets Tajik, Iranian leaders on SCO sidelines

What is on the SCO agenda?

NEW DELHI: With Pakistan’s deputy PM Ishaq Dar in the room, defence minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday delivered a strong message against terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Tajikistan's Dushanbe.Addressing representatives of SCO member countries, Rajnath said terrorism remained one of the biggest threats to peace and development, warning that its impact extended far beyond the loss of innocent lives.“Terrorism not only causes the loss of innocent lives but also disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises society and deprives our youth of the opportunities they deserve,” the defence minister said.The defence minister stressed that terrorism could not be justified under any circumstances and called for a united approach against those who enable it.“There should be no double standards in dealing with terrorism, and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. The entire ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively dismantled,” he said.Rajnath's remarks come days after he reiterated India’s firm position on crossborder terrorism, warning on October 15 that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response.Speaking at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi, he said India’s commitment to dialogue, coexistence and peaceful dispute resolution should not be mistaken for weakness.“Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Rajnath said.He also said that since 2014, the ‘shelf life’ of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of their taking up arms against India.Emphasising the link between strength and peace, Rajnath said India remained committed to peaceful coexistence while staying prepared to deal with threats to its security.“Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge. Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said.On the sidelines of the SCO meeting, Singh held separate meetings with Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref.During his meeting with Rosulzoda, Singh highlighted the longstanding civilisational ties and close people-to-people connections between India and Tajikistan.In a post on X, the defence minister said, "Delighted to meet H.E. Mr Qohir Rosulzoda, Prime Minister of Tajikistan at the commencement of SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe. Underlined the longstanding civilisational ties and deep people to people links between India and Tajikistan."Rajnath also met Aref and shared details of the interaction on X. "Pleasure to meet H.E. Mr Mohammad Reza Aref, First Vice President of Iran on the sidelines of the SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe," he wrote.Rajnath is representing India at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in the Tajik capital, where leaders and representatives of member countries have gathered to discuss regional cooperation.Ahead of the meeting, Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon welcomed Singh and other representatives of SCO member countries at the Palace of the Nation in Dushanbe.According to the ministry of defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening cooperation in culture, connectivity, the economy, innovation, investment and people-to-people ties. Members will also review progress in the organisation's financial and institutional functioning.The ministry highlighted India's contributions across various SCO mechanisms, including initiatives in start-ups, digital public infrastructure and cultural exchanges, saying these offered opportunities to advance practical and mutually beneficial cooperation among member countries.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh delivers a strong message against terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Tajikistan's Dushanbe. He said terrorism remained one of the biggest threats to peace and development, warning that its impact extended far beyond the loss of innocent lives.

Article Title: 'Values that inspired Captain Smit Machchhar':RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat cites flydubai pilot in Vijayadashami speech
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat says Hindu values inspired Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar’s courage to protect lives.

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday linked Captain Smit Machchhar’s courage in preventing a possible plane disaster to Hindu values and traditions, saying these values inspire people to protect human lives and ensure the safety of others.Addressing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh’s annual Vijayadashami celebrations at its headquarters in Nagpur, Bhagwat said Machchhar’s actions reflected values passed down through generations."Since the Hindu society's worldview and nature are inclusive, we must understand that such efforts will only strengthen the emotional unity, goodwill, and good conduct among all of us. It is this very nature and these values, passed down from generation to generation, that inspires Captain Smith Machchar to put his own life in danger and devote himself to protect human lives," Bhagwat said.Machchhar became widely praised after he fought off his co-pilot, who attacked him aboard a Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 people on board. Despite sustaining stab wounds, the captain managed to resist the attack, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene and restrain the co-pilot.Bhagwat said the RSS was working to awaken the Hindu spirit and build a well-organised and strong society."RSS is working to awaken the Hindu spirit and build the entire society into a well-organized and strong society...It is these values that inspired Captain Smit Machchhar to do what he did..."He also said the actions of individuals guided by these values could strengthen national unity and promote harmony across communities.Also Read: ‘Svabodh’ and national unity: Bhagwat’s top quotes from Vijayadashami address as Dhankhar attends RSS event "Driven by this very ethos, what Captain Smit Machchhar did recently was natural. There was no training on what to do in such a situation; her innate tradition and values simply surfaced during that moment of testing. This is the Hindu nature. Consequently, it naturally nurtures and protects the dignity and security of all diversity. This work serves as a constructive force for national unity and global harmony. And this is not something we merely talk about. People do not join the Sangh to listen to speeches; they come first and cultivate the practice of this ethos through their actions..."The RSS chief also spoke about national unity, describing the bond among Indians as unconditional and rooted in a sense of belonging and affection.Also Read: 'Highly inspiring': PM Modi hails Mohan Bhagwat's speech on RSS Sthapana Divas "The Unity of us Bharatiyas - Intrinsic and Unconditional The bond we share with one another and our relationship with Bharat are living bonds, rooted in the heart and therefore unconditional. They are one-sided in nature, as expressed in the words: 'May your glory remain eternal, O Mother; whether we live for a few more days or not'," Bhagwat said.He added that the freedom fighters had demonstrated complete devotion to the nation during the struggle against British rule."Our freedom fighters demonstrated this very spirit of complete and unconditional devotion to the nation. It was this devotion that ultimately compelled the British government to leave Bharat," Bhagwat said.
Article Summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat says Captain Smit Machchhar’s courage was inspired by Hindu values and traditions. He said the actions of individuals guided by these values could strengthen national unity and promote harmony across communities. The RSS was working to awaken the Hindu spirit and build a well-organised and strong society.

Article Title: 'Vote Chori Ki Raasleela’: Youth Congress burns Ravan effigy with Gyanesh's face - watch

NEW DELHI: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) on Monday burned an effigy of Ravan bearing the face of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, demanding his resignation over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission’s functioning and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protest was held at the IYC headquarters on Raisina Road and featured a street performance titled Vote Chori Ki Raasleela, aimed at highlighting allegations of electoral manipulation and questioning the transparency and impartiality of the poll panel, according to a statement issued by the organisation.Addressing the gathering, IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib said the protests would continue until Kumar resigned or was jailed.“Gyanesh Kumar, who is finishing off the democracy and Constitution of the country, cannot save himself. We will continue to protest in different forms. This will continue until he goes behind bars or resigns. He has indulged in ‘vote chori’. Until he is jailed, people of the country will continue to protest,” Chib told news agency ANI.Chib said the Election Commission must be accountable to the public and that the CEC should take moral responsibility for concerns raised over electoral transparency.“Democracy is not merely about holding elections; it is about ensuring that every vote is respected and every citizen's mandate is protected.“When serious questions are raised about electoral transparency, the responsibility of the Election Commission is to provide clear answers and uphold the highest standards of impartiality,” he said.In its statement, the IYC said the effigy-burning was intended to convey its opposition to alleged electoral irregularities and demand accountability from the poll panel.“Through our 'Vote Chori Ki Raasleela' protest, the Indian Youth Congress is sending a clear message that the youth of this country will not allow the sanctity of democracy to be compromised. The burning of the effigy of CEC Gyanesh Kumar represents our anger and our demand for accountability,” Chib said.The protest followed the launch of the IYC’s digital campaign, Digital Ravan Dahan, which invites citizens to identify what the organisation calls the “10 heads of India's Ravan”. According to the IYC, the campaign allows people to register their views through its website and is scheduled to culminate in a virtual Ravan Dahan on Tuesday at 7:30 pm.The IYC has been demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission’s functioning and the SIR exercise. Opposition parties have also raised concerns about aspects of the electoral roll revision process.The organisation said it would continue its protests and public campaigns until its demands for greater electoral transparency and institutional accountability were addressed.
Article Summary: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) burned an effigy of Ravan bearing the face of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi. The protest was held at the IYC headquarters on Raisina Road and featured a street performance titled Vote Chori Ki Raasleela. The IYC has been demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities.

Article Title: ‘Svabodh’ and national unity: Bhagwat’s top quotes from Vijayadashami address as Dhankhar attends RSS event
Article Text:
Mohan Bhagwat invokes Sant Ravidas, stresses diversity and social harmony

Here are the key quotes from Bhagwat’s address:

“India is a land of diversity; our traditional character has been to accept and protect this diversity.”

“When our country was reeling under the attacks of foreign invaders, when they were unleashing terror on those who followed ‘svadharma’ here, and there was an atmosphere of terror, Sant Ravidas spread the message of ‘svadharma nishtha’, social harmony, and devotion. Through the example of his own life, he comforted society at the time and boosted its morale, while upholding its values.”

"Sangh's works, which have been ongoing for 100 years, are something that awakens 'sva'. On the basis of the ethos of that 'sva', efforts are being made to unite India and make it stronger."

"'Svabodh' is reflected in the Preamble of the Constitution - "We, the people of India." That sense of 'we', 'sva' is our emotional bonding with which such a multidiverse country has always been one country, one society, one nation since ancient times."

"Sow a thought and you reap action; sow character and you reap destiny."

"Whether you visit temples, monasteries, or gurudwaras, you will encounter the same knowledge and spiritual guidance. Wherever you go within the Indian ideology, you will find this same wisdom — respect and accept every form of diversity and provide protection to all."

"Need to regulate OTT content; youth absorbing content sans discretion."

"It is due to the lack of such discernment that a serious problem has emerged: drug addiction. It is not that people are unaware that drugs are harmful and potentially fatal. They know this, yet they still develop an addiction, and it has become a serious national problem."

"The recent massive tragedy in Nepal — what happened there is due to the one-sided development in the Himalayan region. This is causing disasters everywhere in the Himalayan region..."

"A storm has blown in from the West that opposes every form of order, propriety, auspiciousness, culture, and human values, seeking to destroy, corrupt, and ruin them. Even developed nations are affected by it. Just look at the news reports from recent days, what is happening in France, Albania, Bangladesh, and Nepal... Our society is vast, and our country is still developing, so challenges persist... Whether it is protesting groups, authorities enforcing law and order, or political leaders, no actions should create conflict, hatred, bitterness, or division within our united society. No matter how strong emotions run, our actions must stay within the boundaries of the Constitution, the law, and civil decorum..."

‘India has been ultimate target of Western regime-change forces’

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday spoke on a range of issues, from the Nepal floods to a "Western-driven wave of regime change" and unrest in countries such as France, Albania, Bangladesh and Nepal.He warned that “India remains an ultimate target” of these forces.Sangh chief Bhagwat addressed the gathering at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur during the organisation’s annual Vijayadashami event, marking its centenary year.Former vice-president Jagdeep Dhankhar attended the event as the chief guest.Also Read: 'Values that inspired Captain Smit Machchhar':RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat cites Flydubai pilot in Vijayadashami speech Also Read: 'Highly inspiring': PM Modi hails Mohan Bhagwat's speech on RSS Sthapana Divas Union minister Nitin Gadkari was also among those present at the event.Earlier in the day, Bhagwat performed shastra puja (weapon worship) at the event.Also Read: India’s diversity, traditional knowledge can help build better world: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
Article Summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke on a range of issues, from the Nepal floods to a "Western-driven wave of regime change" and unrest in countries such as France, Albania, Bangladesh and Nepal. He spoke at the organisation’s annual Vijayadashami event, marking its centenary year.

Article Title: Rubio India visit: Bilateral with Jaishankar, Jamnagar refinery tour & trade deal - whats on agenda
Article Text:
External affairs minister S Jaishankar will meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai on October 20 to discuss ways to enhance the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership between India and the US. (File photo)

Trade deal and energy security in focus

Jamnagar visit and meeting with Ambani

Visit comes amid strains in bilateral ties

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will begin a three-day visit to India on Tuesday, with talks on a proposed bilateral trade deal, energy security and strategic cooperation expected to feature prominently during his meetings with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and other engagements in Mumbai and Gujarat’s Jamnagar.Rubio is scheduled to arrive at Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport at 2.15 pm on Tuesday, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). He will lay a wreath at the Taj memorial to honour the victims of the 26/11 terror attacks before holding bilateral talks with Jaishankar at the Taj Mahal Palace hotel.The two leaders are expected to discuss the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership, including energy, trade and investment, defence, critical and emerging technologies, and the situation in West Asia. Rubio will later attend the “Freedom 250 Reception” at the Jio World Convention Centre to mark the 250th anniversary of US independence. Jaishankar will be the guest of honour.The visit comes as both countries seek to advance negotiations on a proposed trade agreement amid friction over tariffs, energy imports and immigration policies.Speaking in Uzbekistan ahead of his India visit, Rubio said the two sides were close to finalising the agreement."We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that."Rubio also linked the negotiations to Washington’s decision to grant a temporary waiver on certain sanctions related to Russian energy purchases. He said India’s energy requirements and its importance as a US partner were among the factors being considered."These sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countries—India, for example, and others. And so I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy," Rubio said.He added that India had diversified its energy sources but continued to rely on Russian supplies because shifting to alternatives could not happen overnight."You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next. But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States. So we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is," he added.India and the US have been negotiating the proposed trade pact since early 2025, seeking to address tariff disputes, reduce non-tariff barriers and improve market access. Jaishankar recently said the negotiations were nearing a "landing point".Rubio will travel to Jamnagar in Gujarat on Wednesday, where he is expected to visit Reliance Industries’ oil refining complex and meet chairman Mukesh Ambani before returning to Mumbai. The Jamnagar leg of the visit is expected to last around nine hours.The visit comes as Reliance Industries prepares for a planned investment in a Texas oil refinery, bringing energy cooperation and private-sector investment into focus. Officials have not confirmed reports that Rubio may also visit the Vantara animal rehabilitation centre in Jamnagar.Rubio is also expected to engage with Indian business leaders during his visit, although meetings with industrialists Gautam Adani and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran have not been officially confirmed.Rubio’s trip is his second visit to India this year, following his May visit, when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Jaishankar and attended a Quad foreign ministers’ meeting.Bilateral relations have faced strains following US tariffs on Indian goods, disagreements over Washington’s claims about its role in de-escalating the India-Pakistan military conflict in May 2025, and changes to US immigration policies, including higher H-1B visa fees.The two sides are also expected to exchange views on the West Asia crisis and regional stability. Rubio’s visit follows his meetings with Central Asian foreign ministers in Uzbekistan, where he promoted US trade, security and investment ties with the region.
Article Summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will begin a three-day visit to India on Tuesday. He will meet External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and other engagements in Mumbai and Gujarat’s Jamnagar. Talks on a proposed bilateral trade deal, energy security and strategic cooperation are expected to feature prominently.

NEW DELHI: Who really controls the Lawrence Bishnoi network while its notorious kingpin is confined to a high-security cell inside Gujarat's Sabarmati jail? A parallel group comprising Aarzoo Bishnoi, Shubam Lonkar and Randeep Malik handles planning, financing and target selection. Gangster Goldi Dhillon was also part of it but went underground after FBI launched Operation Hardball.Operating from the US, Canada and parts of Europe, the command structure oversees digital intimidation and field executions, directing local recruits through Signal, Instagram and WhatsApp.Also Read: How does gangster Lawrence Bishnoi operate his network from jail? "Operating from deep within international safe havens, these higher-tier masterminds provide the strategic oversight, financial backing and cross-border protection that shield the network's mid-level lieutenants," an investigator said.Pandit, their main public mouthpiece, posts gang manifestos and extortion warnings on social media.A native of Panipat, he travelled to US via Canada a year after Sidhu Moose Wala was killed. Himanshu recently claimed responsibility for a drive-by shooting targeting Haryanvi singer Diler Kharkiya's Range Rover in Sonipat and rival gangster Vinod Kana's killing outside Hisar court complex on Aug 20.Also Read: Extortion is passe, Lawrence Bishnoi gangsters target Bollywood to show who's boss While Tyson issues online warnings to public figures, Hari drives ground-level extortion, and Harman coordinates overseas logistics through local executioners.This distributed chain of command explains why an intercontinental dragnet led by FBI and its global allies has failed to paralyse the syndicate. Barely weeks after Operation Hard Ball, Lawrence's network issued warnings to actor Aamir Khan and Rajasthan politicians over alleged cultural slights.

Article Title: ‘Deliberately breached bonds’: Court extends Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka’s custody by 2 days

NEW DELHI: A special executive magistrate (SEM) on Monday extended the judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka by two days, rejecting fresh sureties furnished by their counsel. The hearing was held before the new magistrate, SEM Ritu Raj, after the previous magistrate recused citing a threatening message. An FIR was registered to investigate that matter.In the order, the SEM observed that the duo had “deliberately” breached the bonds furnished on Oct 11 and committed a breach of peace soon after. Their assurance that they would not repeat the offence did “not inspire confidence”, the order said, citing material submitted by the investigating officer. It also flagged their “habitualness in calling protests at de-notified areas” and said they had shown “no respect for law”. The magistrate rejected the two fresh sureties after personally questioning them.The magistrate rejected the two fresh sureties after personally questioning them. The order noted an “apparent mismatch between one surety’s photograph on the bond and his Aadhaar card,” while, over second surety, the SEM noted, he could not provide basic details, including parentage and address, of Das, with the magistrate concluding that “neither surety had sufficient control” over the activists to ensure their presence before the authorities. Delhi Police sought a further five to seven days of judicial custody, citing an “imminent threat to public order” following an anonymous WhatsApp message allegedly sent to the previous magistrate. The IO also accused the duo of mobilising people to assemble at “de-notified” protest sites through social media and breaching their Oct 11 undertaking.Advocate Abhik Chimni, representing the duo, contested the grounds for continued detention, arguing that the police application did not establish any specific apprehension that the activists would repeat the alleged offence. He maintained that the duo had made no fresh calls for protests after Oct 10 and had gone to Jantar Mantar individually. The defence also assured the magistrate that they would not repeat the alleged conduct and sought their release.“The order will be challenged,” Chimni said.The duo was earlier apprehended at the IGI Airport on Oct 10, along with Abhijeet Dipke, ahead of the planned protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged irregularities in the SIR process. They were subjected to preventive proceedings under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). They were released the same day after furnishing peace bonds of Rs 50,000 each, but were detained again on Oct 13 over their alleged attempt to stage a Tiranga protest at Jantar Mantar.Dipke, meanwhile, was detained Friday and subsequently arrested and placed under preventive arrest the next morning. He was granted bail on the condition that he will not “breach peace” for a year. After Ranka’s and Das’ custody was extended, Dipke posted on X, “Ashu and Saurav’s first crime was waving the Tiranga at Jan-tar Mantar. Their second crime? Refusing to back down. Even after five days in jail, they walked into court with smiles on their faces, their spirits unbroken. ”
Article Summary: CJP activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka extended judicial custody by two days. The hearing was held before the new magistrate, SEM Ritu Raj, after the previous magistrate recused citing a threatening message. Delhi Police sought a further five to seven days of judicial custody, citing an ‘imminent threat to public order’

Article Title: India-New Zealand FTA kicks in: Zero duty, more opportunities - what's in it for India?
Article Text:
India - New Zealand trade deal kicks in

What's in it for India?

1. Duty-free access for Indian exporters

2. A boost for MSMEs and small businesses

3. New opportunities for farmers

4. More opportunities for Indian professionals and students

5. Investment, manufacturing and employment

6. Safeguards for sensitive Indian sectors

7. A larger trade partnership

NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force on Tuesday opening up new opportunities for Indian exporters, manufacturers, farmers, professionals and businesses. The agreement provides 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market for all Indian export tariff lines, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%.Signed on April 27, 2026, the pact aims to deepen economic ties between the two countries and double bilateral trade in goods and services to NZ$7 billion (Rs 35,000 crore) by 2030. Negotiations were launched on March 16, 2025, and concluded on December 22, 2025, within nine months.The agreement is India's 17th operational FTA and the seventh trade pact to come into force in the past five years. It covers goods, services, investment, agriculture, skills and mobility, while retaining safeguards for sensitive sectors.All Indian goods can enter New Zealand duty-free, giving Indian exporters a competitive advantage and placing them on a level playing field with New Zealand's other FTA partners.Textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, automobiles and auto components, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, agricultural products and processed foods are among the sectors expected to benefit.Duty-free access for wooden logs, coking coal and metal waste and scrap will strengthen manufacturing and MSME supply chains. Streamlined regulatory processes are expected to benefit pharmaceutical and medical device industries.The agreement opens New Zealand's market to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), women-led businesses, start-ups, artisans and first-generation entrepreneurs.Zero duties and faster customs processes are expected to reduce landed costs and help Indian businesses expand their customer base. Cooperation will improve access to trade-related information and links with New Zealand's small and medium enterprise ecosystem, with particular attention to businesses owned by women and young people.New Zealand has also committed to facilitating the registration of Indian geographical indications (GIs), creating opportunities to protect products associated with rural artisans and traditional industries.The Agricultural Productivity Partnership will bring technology, training and global best practices to Indian agriculture, extending cooperation beyond tariff concessions.Dedicated action plans for apples, kiwifruit and honey will support better orchard management, reduce post-harvest losses and improve productivity and farm incomes. Cooperation will also cover horticulture, forestry, livestock and fisheries.New Zealand will provide technical assistance to establish Centres of Excellence for kiwifruit, apples and honey. Phase I sites for kiwifruit centres have been identified at Pfutsero in Nagaland and Magra in Uttarakhand. Two apple centres are proposed in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, while honey centres are envisaged in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.Tariff rate quotas for apples, kiwifruit and Mānuka honey are linked to the delivery of action plans and overseen by a Joint Agriculture Productivity Council, linking market access with farmer welfare.New Zealand has offered market access in around 118 services sectors and Most-Favoured-Nation commitments in about 139 sub-sectors, its most extensive services offered under any trade agreement to date.For the first time, dedicated access has been provided for health and traditional medicine services, including Ayurveda, yoga and other AYUSH systems.Indian youth and professionals will have access to 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas and 1,000 Working Holiday visas annually.There will be no numerical cap on Indian students. Post-study work rights will extend to three years for STEM bachelor's and master's graduates and up to four years for doctoral scholars.New Zealand has committed to facilitating $20 billion in investment into India over more than 15 years.The investment is expected to benefit agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and start-ups, supporting innovation, entrepreneurship and employment generation under the Make in India vision.Provisions covering duty-free inputs, bilateral cumulation, customs facilitation and investment promotion could encourage deeper integration into value chains and improve investment conditions.Dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions to protect farmers, dairy producers, fisherfolk and rural communities.Rules of Origin, a bilateral safeguard mechanism and anti-circumvention provisions aim to ensure that benefits reach genuine Indian exporters.Bilateral trade fell about 11% to $1.15 billion in 2025-26, from $1.3 billion in the previous fiscal year. India's exports stood at $566.51 million, while imports were $589.1 million, leaving a trade deficit of $22.59 million.The FTA seeks to reverse the limited scale of trade and expand economic engagement. The first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off at the entry-into-force ceremony, with further product flag-offs planned across agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather.Commerce minister Piyush Goyal said that the agreement would create opportunities for exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers and women entrepreneurs. The pact also supports India's strategic partnership with New Zealand and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, with its success ultimately depending on businesses converting improved market access into actual trade and investment.
Article Summary: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force on Tuesday. The agreement provides 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market for all Indian export tariff lines, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%. The pact aims to deepen economic ties between the two countries.

NEW DELHI: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi 's long-running feud with Salman Khan brought actor Tiger Shroff into the spotlight on Sunday after gunmen opened fire at his car in Mumbai's Juhu. Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries.Shroff's driver, Firdaus, and another person were injured in the October 18 attack, which prompted a police investigation into the identity of the assailants and their motive.A message attributed to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing and linked it to Shroff's association with superstar Salman Khan. The message also warned others in the film industry against working with Salman.The attack is the latest in a series of incidents involving threats and violence allegedly linked to the Bishnoi network against Bollywood personalities and others associated with Salman Khan.The Bishnoi gang's message after the incident linked the attack to Tiger Shroff's professional association with Salman Khan. It claimed that Shroff had been warned earlier but had ignored the warning.The message stated: "Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next."In an audio message released after the attack, a man identified as Anil Pandit threatened Salman Khan and his family, warning the actor against relying on his security and demanding an apology to Lawrence Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community."Listen to me carefully, Salman Khan. If you don't apologise to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won't even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind. Don't think that you are in security and nothing will happen to you," Pandit said in the audio message.The message also warned rival gang members against using the group's name to gain attention. It appeared to be aimed at intimidating not just Shroff but others in the film industry who work with Salman Khan.The authenticity of the messages and the gang's claimed role in the attack remain subject to police verification.The dispute involving the Bajrangi Bhaijaan actor dates back to the 1998 blackbuck poaching case. Lawrence Bishnoi has repeatedly threatened the actor over the case, citing the blackbuck's religious significance to the Bishnoi community.The threats against Salman Khan have continued for years.In June 2022, a threat letter was reportedly found at Bandra Bandstand, where the actor's father, Salim Khan, used to go for walks.The letter warned that Salman Khan would meet the same fate as Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, who was murdered in May that year.In March 2023, Salman Khan's manager received a threatening email referring to Lawrence Bishnoi's threats against the actor. The email also mentioned Goldy Brar, a Canada-based gangster and a close associate of Lawrence Bishnoi.On April 14, 2024, two motorcycle-borne men opened fire outside Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments residence in Bandra. The actor was not injured.Mumbai Police alleged that the shooting was carried out at the behest of the Bishnoi gang. Anmol Bishnoi, Lawrence's brother and a close associate, was among those wanted in connection with the case.Investigators examined the roles of the alleged shooters and their associates, including how the attack was planned.In a separate case, Navi Mumbai Police filed a chargesheet in 2024 alleging that members of the gang had been offered Rs 25 lakh to attack Salman Khan.According to the police, the plan included targeting him during a film shoot or while he was travelling to his Panvel farmhouse.The case also highlighted the role of people allegedly involved in surveillance and planning, beyond those who directly carried out an attack.The threats surrounding Salman drew further attention after former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique was shot dead on October 12, 2024.Siddique, a three-time MLA and Nationalist Congress Party leader, was killed outside the office of his son, Zeeshan Siddique, in Bandra East.A social media post linked to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the murder and warned those helping Salman Khan. Police investigated the alleged links.On February 1, 2026, gunmen opened fire outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence in Juhu.A post attributed to people linked to the Bishnoi network claimed responsibility and threatened further violence if its demands were ignored.Mumbai Police and the Crime Branch investigated the shooting, including the suspected attackers and their alleged links to the network.How the Bishnoi network operatesThe Lawrence Bishnoi network's alleged modus operandi involves different people handling the planning and execution of attacks.Police investigations have examined suspected surveillance, recruitment of shooters, weapons supply, communication between associates, and arrangements for transport and escape.In the 2024 case involving Salman, police alleged that the attackers had gathered information about the actor's movements and locations over an extended period. Investigators also looked into the roles of several people suspected of helping plan the attack.The network led by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi has also been linked to attacks beyond India, including incidents in Canada and the UK.These include multiple shootings at comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Canada, which drew attention to the gang's overseas reach.In November 2025, news agency PTI reported that the National Investigation Agency arrested Anmol Bishnoi after his deportation from the United States.He was wanted in cases including the murder of Baba Siddique and the firing outside Salman Khan's residence.Anmol is Lawrence Bishnoi's brother and a close associate.Mumbai Police are investigating the firing to identify the attackers and establish the motive.Officers are examining CCTV footage and forensic evidence, while checking the authenticity of messages attributed to Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu.Investigators are also looking into whether Shroff had received any threats before the incident.The probe will need to establish whether the attackers acted on behalf of an organised group or whether someone claimed responsibility after the shooting to exploit the incident.For now, the alleged Bishnoi gang link remains under investigation.
Article Summary: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi's long-running feud with Salman Khan brought actor Tiger Shroff into the spotlight on Sunday. Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries. The attack is the latest in a series of incidents involving threats and violence allegedly linked to the Bish noi network against Bollywood personalities.

Article Title: ‘May compromise security’: Delhi HC upholds IAF decision to withhold details of PM Modi, Manmohan Singh’s foreign visits
Article Text:
The case

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court has upheld the Indian Air Force ’s (IAF) decision to deny access to records of foreign visits undertaken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his predecessor, Manmohan Singh , setting aside a Central Information Commission (CIC) order directing the force to disclose the flight records.Justice Amit Mahajan ruled that the CIC had "erred" in its July 2020 order directing the IAF to disclose Special Flight Returns (SFR-II), even after redacting the names and identifying details of security personnel.The judge observed that removing such details would not necessarily eliminate potential security risks.Justice Mahajan rejected the petitioner's argument that the information was a matter of significant public interest as it concerned expenditure on foreign visits funded by taxpayers.Counsel for the petitioner, Commodore (retired) Lokesh Batra, argued that the request sought details of private individuals who accompanied the prime ministers at public expense, not the identities of security personnel.“The mere fact that public funds have been expended on the foreign visits of the Hon’ble prime minister does not, by itself, justify disclosure of information which may compromise the security arrangements put in place for such visits,” the judge observed.The high court held that once the competent authority (IAF) concluded that disclosing the information could jeopardise national security or the prime ministers' safety, neither the CIC nor the court could override the assessment of the security agencies responsible for their protection.Citing Supreme Court judgments on exemptions under the RTI Act, the court reiterated that the right to information (RTI) is not absolute and must be balanced against other protected interests, including national security and the confidentiality of sensitive information.Justice Mahajan noted that Section 8(1)(a) of the RTI Act exempts information whose disclosure could adversely affect the security or strategic interests of the State, while Section 8(1)(g) protects information whose disclosure could endanger a person’s life or physical safety.Holding that the IAF was justified in invoking these exemptions, the high court allowed the petition and set aside the CIC’s order. It also disposed of all pending applications.The case arose from an RTI application Batra filed on June 5, 2018, seeking details of prime ministers’ foreign visits on IAF aircraft from April 1, 2013, until the date of his application.The IAF provided some information about PM Modi’s foreign travel but stated that Manmohan Singh had not travelled on IAF aircraft between April 1, 2013, and May 25, 2014.However, it refused to provide copies of the Special Flight Returns (SFR), Parts I and II, citing national security concerns and the confidential nature of the records.The IAF maintained that the documents contained sensitive details about the aircraft, aircrew, passengers and Special Protection Group (SPG) personnel accompanying the prime minister. It argued that disclosure, particularly when combined with information already available in the public domain, could reveal details of the prime minister’s security arrangements.After the First Appellate Authority rejected Batra’s appeal in September 2018, he approached the CIC. The commission directed the IAF to provide certified copies of the available and relevant SFR-II records, prompting the force to challenge the order before the high court.During the proceedings, the IAF argued that the records contained interconnected details, including passengers’ designations, appointments, identification numbers, flight references, passenger numbers and agency particulars. It stated that disclosing these details could help identify security personnel, reveal the composition of the prime ministers' entourage and allow inferences about security deployment patterns.
Article Summary: The Delhi high court has upheld the Indian Air Force’s decision to deny access to records of foreign visits undertaken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his predecessor, Manmohan Singh. The court set aside a Central Information Commission (CIC) order directing the force to disclose the flight records.

Article Title: 400-plus Indian-origin scholars, alumni from 27 countries warn against ‘anarchy’
Article Text:
It calls for resolving differences through “debate, discussion, dialogue and dissent” within the constitutional framework

NEW DELHI: Days after competing groups of Harvard-linked Indians took opposing positions on protests against the Election Commission, more than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni associated with universities across 27 countries have issued a statement warning against efforts to erode public trust in constitutional institutions and attempts to replace democratic debate with street confrontation.Titled “Spare India from Anarchy”, the statement carries 402 names, including individuals linked to Harvard, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Oxford, Cambridge, Stanford, Princeton, Yale and Columbia universities, as well as the London School of Economics, National University of Singapore and University of Toronto.The signatories allege that “a frenzy of election denial” and a preference for ‘street over Sansad’ have taken hold in some quarters. They argue that unfavourable election results are being used to question electoral procedures, adverse court rulings to cast doubts on judicial independence and even the armed forces are being drawn into partisan debate.“An unconscionable and devious plan of sowing seeds of doubt in Indian democracy has been hatched,” the statement claims, accusing unspecified groups of turning matters before courts into campaigns on the streets.The intervention follows a public disagreement among Harvard affiliates over the October 10 protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. A group of around 100 Harvard-linked signatories criticised alleged police excesses and detentions, while 44 others subsequently warned against attacks on the credibility of constitutional institutions.The latest appeal widens that dispute beyond Harvard, though it does not name the Election Commission, the SIR exercise or the Delhi protests explicitly.Invoking BR Ambedkar’s warning about the “grammar of anarchy”, the statement says dissent remains essential to democracy but should not become a cover for undermining its institutions. It calls for resolving differences through “debate, discussion, dialogue and dissent” within the constitutional framework.The accompanying document says the signatories are based in, or have studied in, countries across four continents. It also makes clear that the listed university affiliations do not amount to endorsements by the institutions themselves.
Article Summary: More than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni have issued a statement warning against efforts to erode public trust in constitutional institutions. The statement carries 402 names, including individuals linked to Harvard, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Oxford, Cambridge, Stanford, Princeton, Yale and Columbia.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Monday transferred the trespassing case against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to the crime branch, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.This came hours after a Delhi court extended the CJP leaders' judicial custody by two days for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructing police personnel on duty.Along with other CJP workers, they waved the national flag at the site and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive custody.According to their lawyer, their bail sureties were rejected due to a reported mismatch in documents. They will now be produced before the court on Wednesday."Today, when we reached the court, the five-day custody period had ended. On the last date of hearing, the court had stated that it did not find the sureties legitimate enough to be accepted. Today, we produced fresh sureties and brought them to court. They have been detained out of fear that they might go and protest. There is no FIR, no pending case against them in this matter, and no investigation for which they need to be questioned. This is absolutely appalling and deeply disturbing. I cannot remember the last time people were kept in preventive custody under such circumstances. We will pursue the matter legally, but this has been hugely disappointing for all of us," he added.The development came amid allegations by the CJP that the bail proceedings had been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two convenors, who were sent to five-day judicial custody on October 13 following a protest at Jantar Mantar.On Sunday, the special executive magistrate hearing their bail matter claimed that unknown persons were threatening him, following which the police registered a non-cognisable report.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and praised Das and Ranka for remaining defiant despite spending five days in judicial custody."You must be feeling very strong keeping a 26-year-old Saurav Das in jail. You must be feeling very strong beating children on the streets. You must be feeling very strong putting up barricades across Delhi and dragging students on the streets," he said.Dipke claimed that Das and Ranka had gone to Jantar Mantar to wave the national flag but were sent to judicial custody. He also alleged that their court hearings had been repeatedly postponed. "Is this strength? Hiding behind the police, hiding behind the courts, is this Narendra Modi's strength?" he asked.
Article Summary: Delhi Police transfer trespassing case against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to crime branch. Delhi court extends CJP leaders' judicial custody by two days for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue.

Article Title: Manipur on boil again: 3 CRPF troops hurt in IED blast; militants kill 3 villagers amid communal clashes
Article Text:

Bodies placed outside CM's residence

Protests spread, markets and shops shut

Police appeal for calm as operations intensify

NEW DELHI: Three Meitei villagers were killed and three others injured after unidentified armed militants opened fire on a group collecting firewood in Manipur on Monday, officials said. It triggered protests in Imphal, where locals placed two of the victims' bodies outside Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's residence.The attack took place around 9.40 am at Sunulok Hill, ahead of Khongbal in the Tangkhul area, under Sagolmang police station.It came amid a series of violent incidents since Sunday night, including a fatal shooting during a clash between two communities in Thoubal district and an improvised explosive device (IED) blast that seriously injured three CRPF personnel.Addressing the incidents, Manipur Police ADGP Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said security forces had intensified operations and were investigating all three incidents."Police and security forces are taking the matter with utmost concern. Necessary security measures have been put in place and the situation is being very closely monitored," he said.The victims were part of a group of 14 Meitei villagers who had gone to cut and transport firewood when unidentified armed militants opened fire on them, Lhatoo said."Today at around 9:40 AM, unidentified armed militants opened fire on a group of 14 Meitei villagers who were engaged in cutting and transporting firewood ahead of Khongbal, Tangkhul area, the exact spot is Sunulok Hill under Sagolmang police station," he said."In the incident, three individuals succumbed to bullet injuries. Three other individuals have also sustained injuries. The injured have been safely evacuated and are undergoing further medical treatment," he added.The deceased were identified in an earlier account as Arubam Ronil, 35, Lairenlakpam Inaobi, 51, and Kshetrimayum Sushil, 32. Ronil and Inaobi died on the spot, while Sushil succumbed to his injuries at a private hospital in Imphal.The injured were identified as N Suraj, 19, Meisnam Somendro, 53, and K Bosan, 45. Three other people were reported missing in earlier accounts of the attack.An injured survivor told officials, "While we were loading the firewood, we were suddenly fired upon," according to news agency PTI.Police have received inputs about those involved and are investigating the attack. Lhatoo said, "Various inputs regarding the persons involved have already been received. The matter is under thorough investigation, and after due process, we will ensure all necessary action will be taken to punish the perpetrators of such heinous crimes."He said joint teams of police, CoBRAs, CRPF, Assam Rifles and BSF were conducting operations in the area."Even as we speak, operations are on in the area with joint teams of Police, CoBRAs, CRPF, Assam Rifles, and BSF, and more Int-based operations are in the offing on priority," he said."Sniffer dogs and drones are being used, and helicopter surveillance has also commenced," he added.Angry locals brought two of the deceased's bodies to Imphal and placed them outside the main gate of the chief minister's residence in Babupara to protest the continuing violence in the state.Police fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the protesters. The bodies were subsequently taken to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS).Security was tightened around the chief minister's bungalow and along the routes leading to it.Following the demonstration, Khemchand Singh visited the injured people receiving treatment at a private hospital in Imphal but did not respond to media queries.The attack triggered demonstrations at several locations in the state capital. Protesters blocked a road at Khurai Lamlong, while a group of women staged a demonstration at Ema Keithel market.Markets and shops across Imphal shut following the incident, as anger grew over the latest attack.Three CRPF personnel were seriously injured in an IED blast in Kakwa Lamdaibung Lampak, near Singjamei police station. The explosion occurred at 11.41pm on Sunday, according to ADGP Lhatoo."In a second incident around 11.41 PM, an IED exploded at Kakwa Lamdaibung Lampak, near Singjamai PS and 3 CRPF personnel were seriously injured and hospitalised at Raj Medicity," he said.Police were pursuing leads in the case."We are pursuing some leads regarding the incident and are confident that we will be able to take action as per law on the culprits," Lhatoo said.The attack on the firewood collectors followed a separate incident in Thoubal district late on Sunday night. Tension erupted between two communities after unidentified persons allegedly pelted stones during a musical night at Khangabok Pali Bazar, under Thoubal police station.Lhatoo said, "In the first incident last night at around 11:20 PM, tension erupted between two communities following a stone-pelting incident by unidentified persons during a musical night at Khangabok Pali Bazar under Thoubal police station."He said the situation subsequently escalated, drawing in communities from Khangabok and Sangakpham."At around 12.40 AM, one individual succumbed to his injuries; these were bullet injuries, at Raj Medicity, while several others were injured," he said.Additional forces, including the Rapid Action Force, CRPF, Assam Rifles and police, were deployed to the area."Additional forces were immediately rushed into the area, including RAF, CRPF, and Assam Rifles and Police and security forces brought the situation under control at around approximately 1:50 AM today morning, 19th of October," Lhatoo said.He added that police were working to identify those responsible and recover illegal weapons."Efforts are on to identify the accused. Witnesses are being located and questioned, and operations are ongoing to also seize the illegal arms in the area," he said.At least 15 houses belonging to the Kuki community were torched in Chassad village in Kamjong district late on Saturday night, officials said on Sunday. Suspected militants allegedly set the houses on fire, forcing several civilians to flee to forest areas and a nearby Army camp.PTI reported that a Kuki civilian was killed and four others sustained bullet injuries when suspected militants attacked the village earlier on Sunday.Deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the violence in Chassad, expressed grief over the death and concern for the injured village leaders and displaced families. She described the burning of houses as an intolerable crime and said she had directed the district administration, state police and security forces to remain vigilant round the clock, protect civilian lives and property, and ensure those responsible were brought to justice.Police said a joint team of the Assam Rifles, Border Security Force and Kamjong Police had been deployed in the affected area to bring the situation under control.In another separate incident at Kamjong district headquarters on Saturday night, three Tangkhul Naga civilians sustained bullet injuries when rival armed groups belonging to another community attacked the village.Lhatoo said security agencies were coordinating to maintain law and order and prevent further escalation."Manipur Police, in close coordination with the CRPF, BSF, Army, Assam Rifles and other sister security agencies, is working continuously to maintain law and order and prevent further escalation," he said.He added that senior police officials were coordinating with stakeholders to restore normalcy and protect residents."All necessary legal and operational measures will be pursued in the strictest manner to identify those responsible and to bring them to justice," he said.The ADGP appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified information."We appeal to the public to remain calm, exercise restraint, and not take the law into their own hands. People are also requested not to believe or circulate unverified information, rumours, or provocative content on social media, as these may aggravate the situation," he said.He urged residents to cooperate with security forces and report suspicious activity to the nearest police station or the central control room.Manipur has witnessed prolonged violence since May 2023. The latest incidents, involving shootings, an IED blast and arson, have renewed concerns over civilian safety and the challenge of restoring normalcy across the state.
Article Summary: Three Meitei villagers were killed and three others injured after unidentified armed militants opened fire on a group collecting firewood in Manipur. It triggered protests in Imphal, where locals placed two of the victims' bodies outside chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's residence. It came amid a series of violent incidents since Sunday night, including a fatal shooting during a clash between two communities in Thoubal district and an improvised explosive device (IED) blast.

Article Title: ‘Spare India from anarchy’: Over 400 Indian-origin students, academics condemn anti-EC protests

NEW DELHI: More than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni from universities in 27 countries have issued a joint statement condemning the ongoing protests against the Election Commission of India (ECI), describing them as a “plan to sow seeds of doubt in India’s democracy”.Titled “Spare India from Anarchy”, the statement criticises the protests against the poll body."An unconscionable and devious plan of sowing seeds of doubt in Indian democracy has been hatched by weaponising sub judice matters, which is then amplified on the streets by leaning on anarchist forces, which have historically and philosophically never believed in constitutional form of governance. All in the name of saving democracy," the statement said."We remain amazed at the irony of all. But more importantly, as informed people who have stakes in the future of this country and travel the world identifying as 'Indians,' we are deeply anguished at this state of affairs," it added.The signatories highlighted the resilience of Indian democracy and the role of constitutional institutions, stating: "In the seven decades since independence, Indian democracy has proved its resilience repeatedly.Institutions have flourished, checks and balances have functioned admirably, and peaceful transition of power has remained an enduring hallmark."They lamented that "a frenzy of election denial, relentless questioning of constitutional institutions, and a preference for 'street over Sansad'" had gripped certain quarters."Unfavourable election outcomes have led to questions of procedural integrity. Adverse judgements have provoked unfortunate commentary on judicial independence. Even the most apolitical institution in the country -- the armed forces -- has been gratuitously and unjustly entangled in partisan discourse," the statement read.While acknowledging that dissent was essential to democracy, the signatories said they refused to remain "silent spectators to the subversion of democratic apparatus in its guise".They urged social and political forces to resolve differences through "debate, discussion, dialogue and dissent" within constitutional institutions.The signatories are based in or have studied at universities across 27 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Japan and Singapore.Their academic affiliations include the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, Harvard University, Stanford University and the London School of Economics, among others. The statement clarified that these affiliations did not imply endorsement by the respective universities.The protests come amid opposition parties’ allegations of irregularities in elections and questions over the integrity of electoral processes.Last month, The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The report triggered protests by opposition parties and citizens’ groups in several parts of the country, particularly in Delhi, with demonstrators demanding the resignation or removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Kumar, who was appointed an election commissioner in 2024 and became CEC in 2025, has repeatedly faced opposition allegations of electoral irregularities and bias in favour of the ruling BJP.
Article Summary: The statement criticises the protests against the poll body. The signatories are based in or have studied at universities across 27 countries. The protests come amid opposition parties’ allegations of irregularities in elections. They lamented that "a frenzy of election denial" had gripped certain quarters.
