Article Title: 'O Captain, My Captain': Should Congress make room for Amarinder Singh again?
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi named Captain Amarinder Singh as his favourite BJP leader.

Amarinder Singh on his relationship with Congress leadership.

The 'Uncle Amarinder' connection

Amarinder's BJP discontent

The political career of Captain Amarinder Singh.

From a 77-seat victory to a bitter exit

Sachin Pilot kept the door open to Amarinder Singh's return to the Congress.

Pargat Singh's leadership test

No CM face, but several leadership questions

In June, Amarinder Singh shared that Rahul Gandhi wished him on his birthday.

What could Captain Amarinder's return mean

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Can a party install a new captain, retain the old team and still leave the door open for a former captain who quit the dressing room five years ago? With the leadership chanting 'O Captain! My Captain!' the Punjab Congress seems to be attempting to navigate that question precisely ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.With Pargat Singh at the helm, Raja Warring and Charanjit Singh Channi 'promised' an active role in the campaign; Sachin Pilot has also left the door open to Captain Amarinder Singh 's possible return. Can Congress accommodate its old captain without unsettling the new captain and the team?Congress general secretary Sachin Pilot, the party's Punjab in-charge, on October 15 offered a line that will keep speculation alive: "Politics mein 'kuch bhi ho sakta hai' (anything is possible in politics)."Asked about the possibility of former Punjab chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh returning to Congress, Pilot praised him as a leader who had served Punjab "well" and was "a man of a very tall stature". He clarified, however, that he had not spoken to Captain Amarinder about his political plans."I've not spoken to him personally about what his future plans are about joining or leaving any party," Pilot told PTI Videos.The remark came less than a fortnight after Congress appointed former India hockey captain Pargat Singh as Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) president, replacing Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on October 2. It also followed Amarinder's public criticism of the BJP, the party he joined in 2022, over its handling of Punjab.So, is Congress merely acknowledging political speculation, or could the old captain's name return to the party's calculations? And if he does return, where would he fit in a state unit that has just changed leadership and is yet to name a CM face?The latest speculation began with an unexpected public greeting. On August 6, during an Instagram 'Ask Me Anything' session with students, leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi was asked to name his favourite BJP politician."Captain Amarinder Singh, definitely. I get along with him, he's cool and he is an expert on military history, so I like him quite a lot," Rahul Gandhi said, before adding: "Hello, Uncle Amarinder!"The former CM responded that his personal relationship with the Gandhi family would remain, but his political commitment was to the BJP. In a September interview with The Tribune, he said he remained fond of Rahul, Priyanka and Sonia Gandhi, while distinguishing personal relationships from politics."My personal relationship with the Gandhis will always be there, but my political commitment is to the BJP," he said."If tomorrow I tell Rahul, Priyanka or Sonia personally that I'll be there for them no matter what, I mean it and I'm happy to help," he added.The indirect exchange was notable because Amarinder Singh's departure from Congress in September 2021 followed a bitter confrontation with the party's state leadership. "When you've been with somebody for fifty years, they remain your party. I never asked to leave them; they asked me to leave," Captain Amarinder Singh said recently.The former chief minister's recent criticism of the BJP has provided the immediate backdrop to the comeback speculation.In an interview published by The Tribune on September 25, Amarinder said the BJP had not consulted him on Punjab politics or policy despite his long experience in the state."I haven't had a single meeting on Punjab policy or politics with them in the last five years," he said.He was more direct about his decision to join the party: "I have gained nothing by joining BJP."Amarinder also argued that the BJP did not adequately understand Punjab and should consult leaders familiar with the state's political and social realities. He advocated an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal, pointing to the BJP's historical position as the junior partner in that relationship.In the same interview, he described himself as going through "difficult times", without elaborating.Yet he has also made clear that dissatisfaction does not automatically mean departure. Amarinder Singh said it was his duty to tell the BJP what he thought about Punjab and that criticising the party's approach did not mean he was quitting.Captain Amarinder Singh's record in Congress spans decades, including two terms as Punjab CM, from 2002 to 2007 and from 2017 to 2021.In the 2017 assembly election, Congress won 77 of Punjab's 117 seats under his leadership, returning to power after a decade. But the relationship between Amarinder Singh and the state leadership deteriorated, particularly amid his prolonged confrontation with Navjot Singh Sidhu.Sidhu became Punjab Congress president in July 2021. The conflict intensified over leadership and the government's handling of election promises. On September 18, 2021, Amarinder resigned as chief minister after the Congress high command called a meeting of the party's legislators to discuss leadership.He subsequently left Congress and launched the Punjab Lok Congress (PLC). In the 2022 assembly election, the PLC allied with the BJP, but the alliance failed to win a seat for Amarinder Singh's party. AAP swept the election with 92 seats, while Congress was reduced to 18.Amarinder joined the BJP in September 2022, and his PLC was merged with it.The electoral record provides the context for the renewed speculation, but it does not establish that bringing Amarinder back would reverse Congress's fortunes. The party's 2022 defeat followed a wider political shift in Punjab, including AAP's rise and Congress's internal divisions.Meanwhile, Pargat Singh's appointment has put a new leader at the head of a state unit that has repeatedly struggled with factional disputes. A former India hockey captain and three-time MLA from Jalandhar Cantonment, he was associated with Sidhu during the 2021 confrontation with Amarinder Singh and had publicly questioned the previous government's delivery on election promises.Pilot called Pargat a "unifying captain", saying the new president has reached out to state leaders and received public support. He has also invoked the team metaphor to describe Congress's approach to the election."You are one captain who's got a fantastic team, and the captain is only as strong as his team," Pilot said he had told Pargat. His appointment, replacing Warring as state chief, was particularly important in the backdrop of an internal tussle between Warring and Channi camps.Punjab Congress has spent months grappling with a bitter power struggle between the camps of state chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and former CM Charanjit Singh Channi. The feud spilled into public view through rival sloganeering, poster wars, clashes at party events and boycotts during visits by then state in-charge Bhupesh Baghel. The high command's July compromise, retaining Warring while appointing Channi to head the campaign committee, failed to end the friction. After Sachin Pilot replaced Baghel as Punjab in-charge in September, Warring eventually resigned on October 2, and Pargat Singh was appointed the new state chief.With the Congress leadership now sending the open-door signal to Captain Amarinder, the question is how Pargat's team would accommodate a strong-headed former CM with a history in the party.Moreover, the issue is not limited to Amarinder Singh. In the upcoming months, Congress must also manage the transition from Warring, who led the state unit from April 2022 until October 2026.Congress has also decided against projecting a CM face for the 2027 Punjab election.Pilot said the party would fight as a team and decide who should lead the state after securing the mandate, following consultations with workers, leaders and MLAs."We are fighting together as a team. Let the team win. And then we'll decide who gets to do what job," he said.The party has several experienced leaders, including Partap Singh Bajwa, Sukhjinder Randhawa, Charanjit Singh Channi and Warring. Pargat's appointment adds a new organisational chief to that mix, while the question of Amarinder's possible return remains unconfirmed.For the high command, the practical issue would be defining the role of each leader without undermining the other.Amarinder Singh's long tenure in Punjab politics, his experience as CM and his association with national security and border-state issues are part of his public political profile. A return could give Congress another experienced voice in its campaign, while his criticism of the BJP could offer a new line of political debate. The Congress may gain from his name, polularity and political history but it is unlikely that he would have any active role owing to his age.But the political costs would depend on the terms of any return. His 2021 exit followed a major leadership confrontation, and Pargat was part of the state leadership aligned with Sidhu during that period. Reconciliation would therefore involve not just Amarinder Singh and the Gandhi family, but a state unit whose leadership has changed since he left.It would also raise questions about the position of leaders who remained with Congress through the subsequent elections and organisational changes. Warring's emphasis on youth representation, Pargat's task of consolidating the state unit and Pilot's insistence on collective leadership all point to issues that would need to be addressed.For now, there is no confirmed proposal to bring Captain Amarinder back, no announced role for him and no indication that talks have taken place or are under way.Pilot's "anything is possible" may keep the question open, but the party's immediate task remains to get the current team working together before Punjab votes in 2027.
Article Summary: Sachin Pilot has left the door open to Captain Amarinder Singh's possible return to the Congress. The former Punjab chief minister left Congress in September 2021 after a bitter confrontation with the party's state leadership. Can Congress accommodate its old captain without unsettling the new captain and the team? Where would he fit in a state unit that has just changed leadership and is yet to name a CM face?

Seven shots were fired at the vehicle, injuring his driver, Firdaus, and a passerby identified as Umesh Charan.One of the videos circulating on social media captures the firing incident, with three men involved in the attack. Two of the assailants approached the vehicle on foot while a third waited on a motorcycle to facilitate their escape.The attackers opened fire as Shroff’s car was slowly moving out of the venue. The firing took place around 350 metres from Juhu police station.Another video shows Shroff switching seats with his driver after the shooting. A woman can be heard urging the actor to leave the spot, saying, “Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger”.The actor took control of the vehicle to rush his injured driver to hospital. Shroff and Firdaus were subsequently taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle for medical attention.The footage provides a glimpse of the immediate aftermath of the firing, as those present at the scene reacted to the incident.Shroff escaped without any bullet injuries, although he sustained minor abrasions from shattered glass. His driver suffered a gunshot wound to his left hand, while Charan sustained bullet injuries to his chest. Both were taken to hospital for treatment.In another purported video that went viral on social media, the gun appears to jam as the shooter attempts to fire the sixth shot. The other shooter then fires two more rounds, taking the total number of shots fired to seven.The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has been linked to claims of responsibility for the shooting through a social media post and a voice note attributed to individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu. Police are verifying these claims and investigating the motive behind the attack.Also read - 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Khan in chilling audio MEanwhile, doctors said Charan was stable but required surgery. Firdaus was also being treated for his gunshot injury.An eyewitness who was present in the area described how the assailants positioned themselves before opening fire at Shroff’s vehicle.Rakesh Kumar, an autorickshaw driver, told ANI that three individuals were involved in the incident. According to his account, one person was on a motorcycle while two others were standing outside, with one near the gate and another positioned slightly ahead of it.Recalling the sequence of events, Kumar said, "I drive a rickshaw here in Mumbai... I arrived around 7:00 PM to take my vehicle out... There were three individuals involved: one was on a motorcycle, while two others were standing outside - one near the gate, and another positioned slightly ahead of it. When the shooting began, one person opened fire from the front, targeting the specific seat where Tiger Shroff was sitting. .. another person, the one near the gate, fired a shot that struck the driver in the hand. It happened around 7:00 PM..."Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams to investigate the shooting and identify those involved. Juhu police and the Mumbai Crime Branch are examining CCTV footage from the area to establish the suspects’ movements and escape route.The three assailants fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a motorcycle. Police are also investigating whether Shroff had received any threats before the attack.The motive behind the shooting remains under investigation.Also Read: 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Two individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, purportedly took responsibility for the attack through a social media post and a voice note.The message alleged that Shroff had ignored warnings and also threatened people in the film industry who continued to work with actor Salman Khan.Police are verifying the authenticity of the claims and investigating whether the individuals who issued the threats were connected to the shooting. Their claims of responsibility have not been independently established.The incident has prompted concerns over the security of film personalities in Mumbai, following previous firing incidents targeting Salman Khan’s residence and other attacks linked to alleged gang rivalries.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti to seek an update on the investigation and directed the police to take strict action against those responsible.Fadnavis also spoke to Shroff and assured him, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”Police are continuing their investigation to identify the shooters, establish the motive and verify the alleged gang connection.
Article Summary: A series of videos has emerged showing the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area. Video captures the moments when unidentified assailants opened fire at his car and the actor switched seats to take the wheel after his driver was injured. Seven shots were fired at the vehicle, injuring his driver, Firdaus, and a passerby identified as Umesh Charan.

But that did not satisfy the court which threatened sit-in dharna by the judges.If to get a work done for benefit of public, the SC judges, even in lighter vein, feel that dharna is a better option than issuing a mandamus to the govt, then it could have serious implications given the stark contrast between right to expeditious justice and the pendency of more than 95,000 cases in the SC.This is the view expressed by a cross-section of lawyers in lighter vein when TOI sought their responses to Justice Pardiwala's banter.Even if one can tell litigants that they must not complain about the 36,000 cases which are pending 'only' for five years in the apex court which has time and again ruled that right to speedy justice is part of right to life, what would the SC tell the litigants who are waiting patiently for the balance of nearly 60,000 cases?If they decide to enforce their right to speedy justice through dharna at the SC, it would create a law and order situation, which an already stretched Delhi police will find it difficult to handle, the lawyers feared.What about those litigants in the HCs who have been awaiting a hearing in their cases for years together, without expecting a decision? They have been routinely told by the SC to await their chance in the HC and declined then out of turn hearing. maximum such application for a direction for early hearing pertain to the Allahabad HC, where over 12 lakh cases are pending, many for decades. If lakhs of litigants decide to hold dharnas at the HC and its bench at Lucknow, would the police be able to handle the surge of protesters?In the trial courts, the pendency is more than 5.1 crore cases, of which 47 lakh are more than 10 years old and 81 lakh are between 5-10 years-old. NEW DELHI: Three separate juries evaluated entries in the three categories for the award and the panel members acknowledged at the end of the day that the quality of applicants was excellent. Article Title: Manipur violence: CM condemns killing of three civilians, orders tighter security in vulnerable areas
Article Text:

Combing operation launched, helicopters deployed

Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh on Monday condemned the killing of three civilians by suspected militants in the border area of Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts and directed officials to strengthen security in vulnerable areas of the state.The three victims were among a group of Meitei villagers collecting firewood in a forest when unidentified gunmen opened fire on them, officials said.Three others were injured and three people were reported missing.The attack triggered protests in Imphal, where demonstrators placed two bodies outside the chief minister's residence. Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters.Singh chaired a security review meeting attended by home minister Govindas Konthoujam, chief secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur, security advisor Kuldiep Singh, director general of police Mukesh Singh and senior officers from the Army, Assam Rifles, CRPF, BSF and other security agencies.An official statement said the meeting reviewed the state's overall security situation and discussed the previous day's incident in Thoubal district and the latest attack in Imphal East.The chief minister “strongly condemned the killing of innocent civilians by armed miscreants at Nongshum in Imphal East district”, the statement said.Security forces launched a combing operation in the Sunurok hills of Kangpokpi district following the attack, deploying sniffer dogs and drones to search the area.Helicopters were also being used for surveillance, news agency ANI reported.Additional director general of police (law and order) Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said unidentified militants opened fire at around 9.40 am on a group of villagers cutting and transporting firewood near Sunurok hills under Sagolmang police station.“Three individuals died in the incident while three more sustained injuries and they are now under medical care,” Lhatoo said.A joint team comprising police, CRPF, CoBRA, Assam Rifles and BSF personnel was conducting the operation, he added. Mobile checkposts had also been established, while security agencies were closely monitoring the situation.“Police, in close coordination with CRPF, BSF, Army, Assam Rifles and other sister security agencies, is working continuously to maintain law and order, and to prevent further escalation,” Lhatoo said.He assured the public that strict action would be taken against those responsible and appealed to people to exercise restraint.Singh later visited the injured at a private hospital and assured them that the state government would cover their medical expenses.The chief minister subsequently chaired a meeting of National Democratic Alliance (NDA) legislators at the chief minister's Secretariat.In a social media post, Singh said the legislators had unanimously condemned the killings and demanded the immediate arrest of those responsible.“The legislators unanimously condemned the killings of three civilians in the strongest terms. They demanded that police and security forces apprehend the perpetrators of the crime immediately,” he said.Protests also erupted at Khwairamband Ima market in Imphal following the attack, with heavy security deployed in the area.The killings came a day after violence in Manipur's Thoubal district left one person dead and several others injured in clashes between two communities.The confrontation reportedly took place during a musical programme at Cherapur in Khangabok.District authorities imposed prohibitory orders in the affected areas, restricting residents from leaving their homes. A few houses and vehicles were also set on fire.The deceased was identified as Laishram Rakesh Singh, who was reportedly struck by a stone during the clashes. Villagers subsequently blocked National Highway 2, demanding justice and action against those involved in his death.In a separate social media post, Singh said he had met representatives of a Joint Action Committee formed over Rakesh's killing.The committee submitted a memorandum raising concerns about the case, and the chief minister assured its members that their demands would be examined and appropriate action taken under the law.
Article Summary: Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh condemns the killing of three civilians by suspected militants. Security forces launch a combing operation in the Sunurok hills of Kangpokpi district following the attack, deploying sniffer dogs and drones to search the area.

Article Title: Cyber unit flags rise in social media fraud using deepfake videos of PM, ministers to promote fake schemes
Article Text:
Deceptive advertisements on Facebook and Instagram impersonate well-known public figures, including the Prime Minister.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has flagged a rise in financial fraud through deceptive advertisements on Facebook and Instagram that impersonate well-known public figures, including the Prime Minister, finance ministers and chief ministers, to promote fake govt schemes.“Victims are asked to pay purported fees or taxes to receive the benefits of these fake schemes. In some cases, advertisements offer fake cashback rewards through scratch-cards or spin-and-win contests, tricking victims into approving UPI collect requests from fraud merchants and transferring money to fraudsters,” the NCTAU warned on Monday.Ads, majorly on meta platforms featuring manipulated/deepfake videos ostensibly show the public figures announcing and promoting a welfare scheme allegedly intended to provide financial assistance to the needy. The advertisements listing phone numbers either offer financial assistance under a purported welfare scheme or cashback/rewards through scratch-card or spin-and-win offers.Victims are either directed to a phone number/WhatsApp chat or redirected to a fraudulent website through the advertisement in order to claim the funds/benefits of the purported scheme. In many instances, victims receive calls from international numbers, largely Pakistan-based (+92 numbers), claiming that they have been randomly selected to receive the alleged funds.Victims are redirected to a website and are coerced to make repeated payments under the pretext of taxes, processing fees, registration charges, verification fees or other administrative expenses in order to receive the funds and benefits.Victims make multiple payments and suffer substantial cumulative financial losses. In some instances, the victims are redirected to a payment app and induced to enter their transaction PIN on the pretext of receiving the prize money. The transaction, however, results in money being debited from the victim’s account and gets transferred to the perpetrator.NCTAU has asked users to check details of welfare schemes on the official website of the concerned department, before acting on social media advertisements. They have been asked to verify the purpose and recipient of any fee or payment requested in connection with a welfare benefit, as well as identities of the persons claiming to represent the govt, through official channels.“Before approving a UPI collect request or entering a UPI PIN, check the transaction details… A UPI PIN is used to authorise payments, not to receive money,” cautioned NCTAU.
Article Summary: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has flagged a rise in financial fraud. Deceptive advertisements on Facebook and Instagram impersonate well-known public figures, including the Prime Minister.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Monday responded to Congress president and Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge , who wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagging the “unusual delay” in proroguing the Monsoon Session of Parliament, which ended on August 13 but has yet to be formally prorogued."With regard to your observation that Parliament has not been prorogued even though 64 days have passed since the House was adjourned sine die on August 13, I would like to clarify that there is no constitutional requirement prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die," Rijiju, the parliamentary affairs minister, wrote in his letter to Kharge."The mere fact that a House has not been prorogued during such an interval does not, by itself, give rise to any constitutional or procedural impropriety," he added.The minister also cited several instances of similar delays during the Congress-led UPA government, inclduing once in 2008, when Houses took up to 87 days to be prorogued.Rijiju further addressed Kharge’s claim regarding the Constitutional Amendment Bill on delimitation. He said the government had reached out to the Congress, the principal opposition party, several times but approached other opposition parties after the Congress failed to provide dates for a discussion."I wrote to you on March 16, March 26 and April 12 in this regard. I had also discussed the matter with you personally and sought your support and cooperation. I also met Shri Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, to discuss the issue and seek his cooperation. However, despite repeated requests, the Congress party did not provide dates for discussion, following which the government reached out to other political parties," he wrote.Citing this, Rijiju expressed surprise that the demand for consultation was still being raised repeatedly and called for the opposition's "constructive cooperation" rather than a "repetition" of the "same demand."Underlining the government’s “firm willingness” to hold consultations, Rijiju reiterated its commitment to the basic principles of parliamentary democracy and expressed hope that the Congress would play a “constructive role” and not obstruct “important future legislations."

NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Monday said his predecessor and YSRCP president YS Jagan Mohan Reddy is regretting supporting the law on Election Commission (EC) appointments because the poll body now “doesn’t do what he (Jagan) says."Addressing a press conference at his residence in Undavalli, Naidu said: “Earlier, you (Reddy) supported the procedure for appointing the CEC. But now, since the EC does not do what you say, you oppose it. Now you are talking about Gen Z... Gen Z.”Naidu's remarks come a day after Reddy " regretted " supporting the 2023 legislation on the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) when the YSRCP was in power in Andhra Pradesh.Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which the YSRCP had supported at the time, the CEC and the two Election Commissioners are picked by a three-member committee comprising the prime minister, a Union minister and the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition.The committee recommends the names to the President, who formally appoints them.However, the legislation has come under criticism because the government, with two representatives on the committee, already has a majority in the panel. The law has been challenged in the Supreme Court.After meeting the State Election Commissioner on Sunday, Jagan Mohan Reddy urged the Centre to revisit the law and expressed regret for supporting the bill in Parliament.Referring to an Indian Express report that alleged a “rift” within the EC, with CEC Gyanesh Kumar on one side and commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on the other, the former chief minister called for “greater clarity”.“Rather than an exchange of allegations, the public needs clarity on what objections were recorded, what action was taken on them, and how transparently the system functioned,” he told reporters.The report, published last month, has triggered protests in several parts of the country, particularly in Delhi, with demonstrators demanding Kumar’s resignation or removal.Reddy also urged the Union government to restore the original selection committee proposed by the Supreme Court, comprising the prime minister, the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition and the Chief Justice of India (CJI).The government later amended the law, replacing the CJI with a Union minister on the committee.

NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk will visit India from October 21 to 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the two leaders set to review bilateral ties and discuss regional and global issues of mutual interest, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Monday.Tusk will be accompanied by Andrzej Domański, Poland's minister of finance and economy, along with a large business delegation, according to an official statement issued by the government.During the visit, Tusk will hold bilateral talks with PM Modi in New Delhi on October 22. The discussions will cover the full range of India-Poland relations, which were elevated to a Strategic Partnership during PM Modi's visit to Poland in August 2024.The two leaders will also exchange views on regional and global developments of mutual interest, the MEA said.Tusk will also travel to Bengaluru, where he is scheduled to meet business stakeholders, including representatives from the information technology and space sectors.An India-Poland Business Forum will be held in New Delhi on October 22 and in Bengaluru on October 23.The visit is expected to advance cooperation across several areas, including trade and investment, defence, emerging technologies, renewable energy, education, culture and people-to-people ties."The visit will provide the opportunity to further strengthen the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, defence, emerging technologies, renewable energy, education, culture and people-to-people ties," the MEA said in its statement.The visit will also provide an opportunity to deepen the strategic partnership between India and the European Union, it added.This will be Tusk's second visit to India in his capacity as Poland's prime minister. His first visit in the role took place in 2010, during his earlier tenure. He also visited New Delhi in 2017 for the India-EU Summit as president of the European Council.The upcoming visit follows the elevation of India-Poland relations to a Strategic Partnership in August 2024, when PM Modi travelled to Warsaw. The visit marked the first trip by an Indian prime minister to Poland in 45 years.During that visit, the two countries adopted a comprehensive five-year action plan covering areas such as trade and investment, defence, energy, green technologies, agriculture and infrastructure.Ahead of Tusk's visit, Polish finance and economy minister Andrzej Domański outlined plans to expand trade and defence cooperation with India.Speaking to news agency ANI on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, earlier this month, Domański said Poland wanted to strengthen industrial partnerships and increase defence exports to India."We want to develop a strong defence industry. To do this, we would certainly like to maintain good trade relations in defence products with trusted partners like India. Therefore, it is no surprise that we would also like to increase the export of our defence products to India. During the visit, we will bring Polish defence companies to India," Domański said.The minister's remarks came after his meeting with Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal.The upcoming visit will provide an opportunity for the two countries to discuss cooperation in defence and other strategic sectors alongside their existing economic and diplomatic engagement.
Article Summary: Polish PM Donald Tusk to visit India from October 21 to 23. Tusk will hold bilateral talks with PM Modi in New Delhi on October 22. Business forums planned in Delhi and Bengaluru. Second India visit as Polish prime minister.Defence and industrial cooperation on agenda.

NEW DELHI: Protesters on Monday placed the bodies of two persons outside Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's bungalow in Imphal after they were killed by suspected militants near the border of Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts.Angry locals brought the bodies to Imphal to protest the violence that has plagued the state since May 2023. They placed the bodies outside the main gate of the chief minister's residence in Babupara.It was not immediately known whether the CM was present at the residence during the protest.Police fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the protesters, following which the bodies were taken to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS). One of the injured, identified as Ksh Deven, was stated to be in serious condition, officials said.According to police officials, four others were also injured after suspected militants opened fire on a group of firewood collectors.Three persons are still missing following the incident, which took place at Khongbal Sunurok Uyok in Kangpokpi, a few metres from Nongshum village in Imphal East, they said.The deceased were identified as Arubam Ronil (35) and Lairenlakpam Inaobi (51).They were among 16 people who had gone to the hills near their village around 7 am to collect firewood when they were ambushed, officials said.Earlier on Sunday, at least 15 houses belonging to the Kuki community were torched in a hill village in Manipur's Kamjong district, forcing several civilians to flee to forest areas and a nearby Army camp.According to news agency PTI, a Kuki civilian was killed and four others sustained bullet injuries when suspected militants attacked the village.In a separate incident at Kamjong district headquarters on Saturday night, three Tangkhul Naga civilians sustained bullet injuries when rival armed groups belonging to another community attacked the village.

How a painting estimated at ₹8 crore sold for nearly ₹120 crore

Not all paintings in the world are being sold in crores. But there’s one particular painting titled A Family of Cheetahs in a Rocky Landscape that was sold for nearly Rs 120 crore in London. It created a stir in the world of painting and made headlines. This is the painting attributed to Basawan, one of the most prominent painters associated with Akbar’s court.Back in 1575–80, when Mughal emperor Akbar was building one of the most influential courts in Indian history, Basawan created an extraordinary painting of a family of cheetahs. The painting which was made nearly 450 years ago has survived and has seen several empires rise and fall. It witnessed the ever-changing artistic tastes and centuries of collecting.In October 2025, the painting made headlines when it was sold at Christie’s in London for £10.245 million (₹119 crore at the time).If you look at the painting, it doesn’t look like a grand royal portrait. The painting’s beauty lies in its remarkably detailed study of animals in their natural surroundings.Yet this intimate glimpse into the wildlife of Mughal India became one of the most valuable paintings of its kind ever sold at auction.According to Christie’s, the sale also set a world auction record for a Classical Indian or Islamic painting. What makes the story particularly fascinating is that the artwork’s importance extends far beyond its extraordinary price, offering a glimpse into the artistic imagination. It shows the royal interests of sixteenth-century India.The painting belongs to a flourishing period of Mughal art. Akbar was an artist who supported a flourishing royal workshop where Indian and Persian artistic traditions came together. Painters working under imperial patronage developed a distinctive style and created masterpieces worth remembering.Basawan was a leading artist from the Akbar period. His work is largely associated with innovation and expressive figures. The cheetah painting, dated to approximately 1575–80, is attributed to him rather than being definitively signed by the artist.What makes this painting unique is its subject. Rather than depicting any royal figure or a scene from a religious book, it focuses on animals in their natural habitat. The composition brings together art and observation.The Mughal fascination with animals was not just decorative. Hunting, falconry and the keeping of exotic animals were part of courtly life. Akbar and other Mughal emperors maintained elaborate courts in which artists recorded people, events, landscapes, plants and animals. Under Akbar’s successor Jahangir, naturalistic painting became prominent, with artists producing remarkably detailed studies of birds and animals.Against this background, a family of cheetahs is an evocative subject. The painting does not simply use an animal as a symbol of royal power; it presents a glimpse of wildlife as a subject worthy of close artistic attention.The artwork went on to become part of the personal collection of Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan and Princess Catherine Aga Khan. Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan (1933–2003) was a diplomat and philanthropist who served as the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees from 1965 to 1977. He was also a collector of unique artwork. The couple acquired much of their collection between the 1960s and the 1980s. Many of the paintings they selected were later studied and published by scholars. They were also put you display.The collection was displayed at Château de Bellerive, their home on the shores of Lake Geneva in Switzerland. The cheetah painting was among 95 works offered at Christie’s London auction on October 28, 2025.Before the auction, Christie’s estimated the cheetah painting at £700,000 to £1 million. Its eventual sale price of £10,245,000, including the buyer’s premium, was approximately 14 times more than its estimate.The result was also the highlight of the wider auction, which totalled £45.76 million, six times its pre-sale estimate. Every lot sold, with bidders registered across 20 countries and four continents, according to Christie’s.
Article Summary: A Family of Cheetahs in a Rocky Landscape, attributed to Basawan, Mughal India, circa 1575-80, sold at Christie’s in London for £10.245 million in October 2025. The painting is one of the most valuable paintings of its kind ever sold at auction. The sale also set a world auction record for a Classical Indian or Islamic painting.
